newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mother says Japan should try child killer as adult.
newsitem.headline: Mother says Japan should try child killer as adult.

text.p: The mother of a 10-year-old girl allegedly killed by a Japanese schoolboy who is also accused of beheading a playmate demanded on Wednesday that the suspect be charged as an adult instead of as a juvenile.
In Japan, under-age criminals are tried by Family Courts at which there are no traditional prosecution proceedings and the emphasis is on rehabilitation rather than punishment.

"It is said the boy has a future and will return to society rectified. But what about the bright future of my daughter?" wrote Kyoko Yamashita, mother of Ayaka Yamashita, who was allegedly killed with a hammer by the suspect in May.
Yamashita made her plea in a letter written to the Asahi Shimbun and published on Wednesday.

In one of the most shocking case of juvenile crime in Japan, a 15-year-old boy was arrested on suspicion for murdering and beheading 11-year-old playmate Jun Hase, and was later accused of three other attacks on schoolchildren, including Ayaka.
The attacks all took place in the western Japanese city of Kobe.
The boy's name has been withheld. If convicted, he faces a maximum sentence of just two years at a juvenile correction centre.

"As the boy wrote himself, if the suspect was an adult, he would probably be sentenced to death. How am I to accept the irrationality that he is protected by the law just because he is a juvenile?" wrote Yamashita.
The suspect had sent a letter to a local newspaper claiming responsibility for the murder of Jun and challenging police to arrest him, in which case he said he was likely to be sentenced to death.
Yamashita said her daughter became a victim because of her kindness. The suspect allegedly asked where he could wash his hands and Ayaka took him to a nearby school.

"I'm very sad that her kindness turned against her...but I strongly believe that I was not wrong in teaching her to be kind to those who need help, not to do things you don't want others to do to you," wrote Yamashita.
"We don't know the boy (suspect)...but I will never forgive an inhumane act of seeing my daughter, talking to my daughter, then killing her in an experiment."
Police said the suspect wrote a note saying he carried out the attacks as a "sacred experiment" to determine the frailty of humans.
